text: Restaurants should be treated as a system of franchise economics, procurement, approved-vendor networks, commissary/distribution, delivery data, foodservice inputs, private-label beverage supply, and labor-saving infrastructure rather than only public restaurant brands.

Franchise procurement platforms remain the strongest validated node because Domino's and Yum evidence shows centralized sourcing and supply-chain coordination can influence franchisee economics and supplier relationships.

Private-label coffee and foodservice beverage supply is a plausible underfollowed node, with Westrock Coffee and Farmer Brothers as initial hypotheses requiring primary-source customer and materiality verification.

TreeHouse Foods should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a second-order private-label/co-manufacturing hypothesis tied to the reported Farmer Brothers asset acquisition, but its restaurant exposure is unproven.

Layer 1 universe is underbuilt outside franchise procurement and coffee/private-label supply; next expansion should deliberately search equipment, automation, software, distributors, packaging, proteins, dairy, oils, compliance, and inspection.
Need current market caps, analyst coverage counts, primary filing evidence, named customer relationships, and commodity margin sensitivity before any Layer 2 validation or ranking upgrade.

Restaurant industry-chain map should prioritize franchisee economics, procurement scale, approved suppliers, commissary/distribution, foodservice distribution, labor productivity, digital ordering, and beverage input systems rather than only restaurant brands.

Highest-probability bottlenecks are procurement platforms, approved-vendor certification, centralized commissary/distribution, labor productivity, contracted commodity access, and digital/loyalty data.

Low-attention supplier value may hide in B2B coffee/tea/extract suppliers, private-label and co-manufacturing, restaurant equipment service, POS/back-office tools, group purchasing, and regional distribution alternatives.
Distribution consolidation is a catalyst to monitor because it may weaken independent restaurant procurement economics and increase demand for alternative distributors and cooperative purchasing.
Evidence of chains moving food inputs from spot markets to contracted pricing is a positive catalyst for franchisee economics and procurement-control theses.
Adoption of smart kitchen, loyalty, app ordering, and store-throughput systems is a key restaurant technology catalyst, especially where labor availability and order speed constrain unit economics.

Need primary-source verification from 10-Ks, 10-Qs, earnings calls, supplier pages, franchise disclosure documents, and customer announcements for WEST, THS, FARM, packaging suppliers, equipment vendors, and restaurant software providers.

Need a broader public-market mapping across distributors, packaging, automation, POS software, coffee/beverage suppliers, co-manufacturers, proteins, dairy, and equipment service before Layer 2B candidate scoring.

DPZ should remain the reference anchor for franchise procurement and vertically integrated commissary/distribution economics in the Restaurants theme; verify latest company filings before using exact center count or margin figures.
YUM should remain a reference anchor for global multi-brand supplier coordination and approved-supplier networks, but supplier-level public-market mappings require named supplier evidence.

WEST belongs in the underfollowed lane as a B2B beverage and private-label coffee/extract supplier candidate, but should not advance beyond hypothesis status until restaurant/QSR/customer materiality and capacity utilization are verified in filings.

THS belongs in the underfollowed lane as a private-label/co-manufacturing and Farmer Brothers asset-acquisition angle, but the restaurant-adjacent link is weak until contract transfer, channel mix, and utilization evidence are found.

FARM is a speculative micro-cap shadow supplier candidate tied to foodservice coffee and direct-store-delivery relationships; liquidity, debt, asset-sale effects, and current customer materiality are gating issues.

Need primary-source filings for WEST, THS, and FARM to verify channel mix, customer concentration, foodservice/QSR exposure, capacity utilization, gross margin, debt, and whether named restaurant or hospitality relationships are current.

Need a broader restaurant supplier universe beyond this chunk, especially restaurant equipment, kitchen automation, POS/back-office software, food safety/compliance, packaging, protein/dairy/cheese suppliers, oils, and group purchasing organizations.
